newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firmer, but strong futures dull buying.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firmer, but strong futures dull buying.

text.p: NWE spot gas oil prices were firmer on Monday but trade was thin as stronger crude and benchmark gas oil futures kept buyers scarce, traders said.
Weaker heating oil barge premiums ahead of the expiry of May IPE futures countered early gains on the May contract.
After the expiry premiums firmed to meet the $2.75 per tonne backwardation of the incoming June contract, but shrank back as stronger NYMEX products boosted the contract into contango.
May IPE futures expired at 1100 GMT $1 up at $171.75 a tonne. A total of 97,100 tonnes of gas oil will be delivered into the May IPE gas oil contract, a source at the IPE said.
Some dealers said they had expected a much larger volume to be delivered into the contract, possibly between 200,000 and 500,000 tonnes.
Diesel cargoes were offered at June IPE +$12-13 with bids around $2 lower while FOD was pegged unchanged at around June IPE +4-5 and Russian valued around June IPE +3.50 cif NWE.
